fields.description: Trade name of the recipient. Compared when matching rows to a note, as in the unamended section.
Note number as originally reported. Identifies which already-filed note this row amends.
Note date as originally reported. Usually falls in an earlier return period.
Corrected note number. May equal the original.
'C' for a credit note, 'D' for a debit note.
Place of supply as 'NN-Name'; only the numeric prefix is retained.
Whether tax is payable by the recipient under reverse charge. Mandatory with no default.
Nature of the underlying supply, from the shared invoice-type label set.
Corrected total value of the note including tax. Non-negative.
Proportion of the tax rate that applies. Emitted as a factor.
Combined tax rate for this line, in percent.

constraints.name: min_exclusive
constraints.description: Must be strictly positive — a zero taxable value is rejected.

fields.description: Corrected taxable value at this rate, excluding tax. Strictly positive.
Corrected cess on this line. Blank is treated as 0.

rules.description: An intra-state supply that nonetheless attracts IGST is only valid as a reverse-charge supply.
rules.message: Reverse Charge must be 'Y' when Note Supply Type is 'Intra-State supplies attracting IGST'.
Reverse Charge must not be 'Y' when Note Supply Type is 'Deemed Exp'.

keys.description: Proportion of the tax rate that applies, as a factor. The reference emits this key ONLY when it is 0.65 and discards every other value, so an unscaled row carries no such key at all. Verified against a file captured from the tool.
Integrated tax. Present on inter-state lines only.
Central tax. Present on intra-state lines only.
State/UT tax. Present on intra-state lines only, always equal to camt.

derivation_notes.gstr1.item_num: Line item number is derived from the rate, not a sequence: num = rt * 100 + 1.
derivation_notes.gstr1.tax_split: Identical to the B2B sections, and gated on the same codes: intra-state when the place of supply equals the supplier's state AND the note supply type is R or DE AND the supplier is not an SEZ unit. Intra-state: camt = samt = round(txval * rt * 0.005 * diff_percent, 2). Inter-state: iamt = round(txval * rt * 0.01 * diff_percent, 2). SEWOP forces every tax amount to 0.
derivation_notes.gstr1.cess: csamt = round(Cess Amount, 2), or 0 when blank. Forced to 0 for note supply type SEWOP.

notes.text: Taxable value must be STRICTLY positive; note value and cess need only be non-negative. Nothing in this table may be negative — a credit note is distinguished by its note type.
Reverse Charge is mandatory with no default, as in the unamended section.
The payload array is keyed 'nt' and the amendment keys are ont_num/ont_dt, but the nature of the underlying supply is still emitted as 'inv_typ' using the shared invoice-type codes.
Nothing requires the revised note to postdate the original, or the revised date to fall in the period being filed — the routine that looks like it enforces date ordering is unreachable.
Numeric cells may carry thousands separators. The reference strips only the FIRST comma, so '1,234,567' reads as 1234; every separator is stripped here.

The reference groups rows into one amendment when EITHER the revised or the original note number matches, then rejects the group on any other disagreement. Grouping here keys on the revised number alone, matching the tool's own declared key.

The recipient's name is NOT sent to the portal. The reference strips cname from this section's envelope in removeCName() before writing the upload file, so the name is captured in the workbook for the filer's benefit only. Verified against a file captured from the tool.

The internal 'diffval' flag never reaches the upload JSON — the reference deletes it alongside the tax-rate factor. This resolves what was previously an open question. Verified against a file captured from the tool.
